text.p: Swiss shares ended higher, overcoming the psychologically important 3,900 point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) on foreign demand.

One dealer said the shares seemed to be increasingly profiting from speculative interest. He said investors were counting on strong advances at the end of the year and the beginning of 1997 in view of the fact that the Swiss market has lagged others.
The SMI was up 18.4 points, or 0.47 percent, to 3,902.5 and the all-share SPI advanced 12.14 points to 2,493.19.
One trader said shares were underpinned by a firming U.S. dollar and a rise in government bond futures.
CS Holding and Electrowatt gained more than one percent and two percent, respectively, on revived rumours that CS Holding was about to sell its 44.9 stake percent in Electrowatt.
CS Holding was up 2.25 francs at 138.75. Electrowatt added 13 francs to 523.
Electrowatt said after the bourse closed that it would spin off its energy business and retain only its industrial activities. The energy business will go on the bourse under the name Watt AG.
UBS bearer shares overcame initial weakness, adding five francs to 1,228.
Roche certificates were sought from foreign investors, jumping nearly one percent to 10,020. Ciba and Sandoz lost around 0.3 percent each.
Among industrials, Alusuisse, SMH and Holderbank profited from recommendations. ABB, Nestle and Sulzer were also among the winners.
Second-tier shares, Valora and Ascom showed strong advances.
